newsitem.title: ERITREA: Italian firm to construct $17.5 mln Eritrea hotel.
newsitem.headline: Italian firm to construct $17.5 mln Eritrea hotel.

text.p: An Italian firm will build Eritrea's first five-star hotel, its Eritrean financiers said.

Tuolde Tesfamariam, manager of Asmara Palace Investment Plc told Reuters in an interview on Thursday: "We signed a contract with CMC (Cooperativa Muratori Cementisti Ravenna) on Wednesday. Excavation work will start on November 15."
The hotel which will be called Asmara Palace Hotel.
"The country needs a five-star hotel. Because investors, businessmen and tourists will be coming", said Tuolde. According to contract terms, the hotel will be ready in 26 months.

Tuolde and his Italian-based company Red Sea General Import & Export own 40 percent of Asmara Palace Investment, the ruling party has a 40 percent stake, CMC has a 10 percent shareholding and Irish firm Bergheihm International, which will manage the hotel, also holds hold a 10 percent stake.
Construction of the 200-room hotel will cost $17.5 million while furnishings will take another $5 million.

Tuolde said he was in discussions with the Eastern and Southern Africa Trade and Development Bank (PTA Bank) for financing to the tune of $5 million. He did not say how the financing for the core $17.5 million would be arranged.
Tuolde and his family own Red Sea Cooperative Hotels, which has built the luxury Gurgussum Beach Hotel outside Massawa on the Eritrean Red Sea coast which he hopes to open in December.
Eritrea became formally independent from Ethiopia in 1993, after the end of a 30-year liberation war in 1991.

The region's potential for tourism was neglected for decades, but since independence, the country is trying hard to build a tourism industry. Massawa, on the Red Sea, was shattered during the war, but is presently undergoing a facelift.
